title.zh: 卷一百一十 志第六十三 禮十三
title.raw: 卷一百一十 志第六十三 禮十三 Volume 110 Treatises 63: Rites 13

sentences.zh: 禮十三

translations.literal: Rites Thirteen
translations.idiomatic: Rites 13

sentences.zh: 〈（嘉禮一）〉

translations.literal: (Auspicious Rites One)
translations.idiomatic: (Auspicious Rites 1)

sentences.zh: ○上尊號儀高宗內禪儀上皇太后皇太妃冊寶儀

translations.literal: ○ The ceremony for conferring an honorific title; the ceremony for Gaozong's abdication; the ceremony for presenting seals and regalia to the empress dowager and the imperial consort dowager
translations.idiomatic: ○ Ceremonies for conferring honorific titles, for Gaozong's abdication, and for presenting seals and regalia to the empress dowager and imperial consort dowager

sentences.zh: 舊史以飲食、婚冠、賓射、饗宴、脤膰、慶賀之禮為嘉禮，又以歲時朝會、養老、宣赦、拜表、臨軒命官附之，今依《政和禮》，分朝會為賓禮，餘如其舊雲。

translations.literal: The old histories took the rites of food and drink, capping and marriage, archery contests for guests, banquets, offerings of raw and cooked meat, and congratulatory celebrations as auspicious rites, and also attached to them the seasonal court assemblies, honoring the aged, proclaiming amnesties, presenting memorials, and appointing officials at the imperial audience; now, following the 《Zhenghe Rites》, court assemblies are classified as guest rites, and the rest remain as before, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier histories classified the rites of dining, capping and marriage, guest archery, banquets, offerings of raw and cooked meat, and congratulatory celebrations as auspicious rites, and grouped with them seasonal court assemblies, honoring the aged, amnesty proclamations, memorial presentations, and appointments made at the imperial audience. Following the 《Zhenghe Rites》, court assemblies are now classified as guest rites; the remainder are treated as before.

sentences.zh: 尊號之典，唐始載於禮官。

translations.literal: The institution of honorific titles was first recorded by the Tang in the offices of rites.
translations.idiomatic: The institution of honorific titles was first entered in the rites offices under the Tang.

sentences.zh: 宋每大祀，群臣詣東上閣門，拜表請上尊號，或三上，或五上，多謙抑弗許。

translations.literal: Under the Song, at each major sacrifice, the ministers went to the Eastern Upper Gatehouse, presented a memorial requesting that an honorific title be conferred, sometimes submitting three times, sometimes five times, and for the most part the emperor modestly declined to grant it.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Song, at each major state sacrifice ministers would go to the Eastern Upper Gatehouse and submit memorials asking that an honorific title be conferred—sometimes three submissions, sometimes five—and the emperor would most often decline out of modesty.

sentences.zh: 如允所請，即奏命大臣撰冊文及書冊寶。

translations.literal: If the request was granted, a memorial was submitted ordering great ministers to draft the text of the patent and inscribe the patent and seal.
translations.idiomatic: If the request was accepted, the court would order senior ministers to draft the patent text and inscribe the patent and imperial seal.

sentences.zh: 其受冊多用祀禮 畢日，禦正殿行禮，禮畢，有司以冊寶詣閣門奉進入內。

translations.literal: Receiving the patent was mostly done on the day the sacrificial rites were completed; the emperor proceeded to the main hall to perform the ceremony, and when the rites were finished, the relevant offices took the patent and seal to the gatehouse and presented them to enter within.
translations.idiomatic: Receipt of the patent usually took place on the day the sacrificial rites concluded. The emperor would proceed to the main hall to perform the ceremony; when it ended, the responsible offices carried the patent and seal to the gatehouse and presented them for entry into the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 建隆四年，群臣三上表上尊號，詔俟郊畢受冊。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jianlong, the ministers thrice submitted memorials requesting an honorific title; an edict ordered that the patent be received after the suburban sacrifice was completed.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianlong 4, 963, the ministers submitted three memorials requesting an honorific title; an edict ordered that the patent be received after the suburban sacrifice was completed.

sentences.zh: 前三日，遣官奏告天地、宗廟、社稷，遂為定制。

translations.literal: Three days beforehand, officials were dispatched to report to Heaven and Earth, the ancestral temples, and the altars of soil and grain; this then became the established regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Three days beforehand, officials were dispatched to report to Heaven and Earth, the ancestral temples, and the altars of soil and grain; this thereafter became standard practice.

sentences.zh: 其儀：有司宿設崇元殿仗衛，文武百官並集朝堂之次，攝太尉奉冊於案，吏部侍郎一員押，司徒奉寶於案，禮部侍郎一員押，以五品、六品清資官充舉冊、舉寶 官，皆承之以匣，覆之以帕，俱詣殿門外之東、太尉之前。

translations.literal: The ceremony: the relevant offices set up overnight the guard of honor at Chongyuan Hall; civil and military officials all assembled in the outer court; the acting Grand Commandant presented the patent on a table, with one vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel escorting it; the Minister of Education presented the seal on a table, with one vice minister of the Ministry of Rites escorting it; fifth- and sixth-rank officials of pure qualification served as patent-bearers and seal-bearers; all carried them in cases covered with cloth, and all proceeded to the east of the hall gate, before the Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: The procedure was as follows. The relevant offices set up the guard of honor at Chongyuan Hall overnight. Civil and military officials assembled in the outer court. The acting Grand Commandant placed the patent on a table, escorted by a vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel; the Minister of Education placed the imperial seal on a table, escorted by a vice minister of the Ministry of Rites. Fifth- and sixth-rank officials of pure qualification served as patent-bearers and seal-bearers, each carrying the object in a case covered with cloth. All proceeded to the east side of the hall gate, before the Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 大樂令帥工人入就位，諸侍衛官及宰執、兩製、供奉官等立於殿階下香案前左右，如常入閣儀。

translations.literal: The Director of Great Music led the musicians in to take their places; all guard officers, chief ministers, Hanlin academicians, and attendance officials stood to the left and right before the incense table below the hall steps, as in the usual ceremony for entering the privy council.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Great Music led the musicians to their stations. Guard officers, chief ministers, Hanlin academicians, and attendance officials took their places to the left and right of the incense table below the hall steps, following the usual privy-council entry ceremony.

sentences.zh: 侍中奏中 嚴外辦，所司承旨索扇，扇上，皇帝袞冕，禦輿出自西房，樂作，即御坐，扇開，樂止。

translations.literal: The Palace Attendant reported that the inner vigil was complete and the outer preparations ready; the relevant offices received the order and requested the fans; when the fans were raised, the emperor in full regalia came forth in the imperial carriage from the west chamber; music sounded; he immediately took the throne; when the fans were opened, the music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Attendant announced that the inner vigil was complete and outer preparations ready. On imperial order the attendants raised the fans. The emperor, in full ceremonial regalia, emerged in the imperial carriage from the west chamber to music, took the throne, and when the fans were opened the music ceased.

sentences.zh: 符寶郎奉寶如常儀，禮直官、通事舍人分引太尉以下文武群官應北面位者， 各就橫行位，太常卿於冊案前導至丹墀西階上少東，北向置訖。

translations.literal: The Seal and Talisman Attendant presented the seal according to usual ceremony; ritual officers and Communications Chamberlains separately led the Grand Commandant and below, all civil and military officials who were to take north-facing positions, each to his transverse rank; the Minister of Rites, before the patent table, guided it to slightly east on the western steps of the red terrace, placed it facing north, and finished.
translations.idiomatic: The Seal and Talisman Attendant presented the seal in the usual manner. Ritual officers and Communications Chamberlains led the Grand Commandant and all civil and military officials assigned north-facing positions to their transverse ranks. The Minister of Rites guided the patent table from before it to a spot slightly east on the western steps of the red terrace and set it down facing north.

sentences.zh: 太尉、司徒、吏部禮部侍郎各入本班立定，典儀讚百官再拜舞蹈，三稱萬歲，又再拜起居訖，又再 拜，分班序立。

translations.literal: The Grand Commandant, Minister of Education, and vice ministers of Personnel and Rites each entered their proper ranks and stood fixed; the master of ceremonies praised the officials to bow twice and perform the dance, thrice shout "Ten thousand years!," bow twice again and report on health, bow twice again, and stand in ordered ranks by division.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Commandant, Minister of Education, and the vice ministers of Personnel and Rites each took their proper ranks. The master of ceremonies directed the officials to bow twice and perform the dance, shout "Long live the emperor!" three times, bow twice again and report on the emperor's health, bow twice more, and stand in order by division.

sentences.zh: 禮直官引太常卿隨行，吏部侍郎押冊案以次序行，太尉從之，禮部侍郎次押寶案行，司徒從之，詣西階，至解劍褥位。

translations.literal: Ritual officers led the Minister of Rites to follow; the vice minister of Personnel escorted the patent table in order of march, the Grand Commandant following; the vice minister of Rites next escorted the seal table in march, the Minister of Education following; they proceeded to the western steps, to the place for removing sword and shoes on the mat.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual officers led the Minister of Rites forward. The vice minister of Personnel escorted the patent table in procession, followed by the Grand Commandant; the vice minister of Rites next escorted the seal table, followed by the Minister of Education. They proceeded to the western steps, to the mat where sword and shoes were removed.

sentences.zh: 其讀冊中書令、讀寶侍中，候 冊案將至，先升於前楹間第一柱北對立。

translations.literal: Those who read the patent, the Director of the Secretariat, and those who read the seal, the Palace Attendant, waited until the patent table was about to arrive, then first ascended and stood facing each other north of the first pillar between the front columns.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of the Secretariat, who was to read the patent, and the Palace Attendant, who was to read the seal, waited until the patent table was approaching, then ascended first and stood facing each other north of the first pillar between the front columns.

sentences.zh: 太尉解劍、脫舄訖，吏部侍郎押冊案先升，太尉從升，當御坐前。

translations.literal: The Grand Commandant removed his sword and took off his shoes; when finished, the vice minister of Personnel escorted the patent table up first, the Grand Commandant ascending after, stopping before the imperial throne.
translations.idiomatic: After the Grand Commandant removed his sword and shoes, the vice minister of Personnel escorted the patent table up first, with the Grand Commandant following, until they stood before the imperial throne.

sentences.zh: 太尉搢笏，北面奉冊案稍前跪置訖，俯伏，興，少退，東 向立；

translations.literal: The Grand Commandant inserted his tablet, faced north, presented the patent table, advanced slightly, knelt and placed it; when finished he prostrated himself, rose, retreated a little, and stood facing east;
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Commandant inserted his tablet, faced north, advanced the patent table slightly, knelt and set it down, prostrated himself, rose, stepped back a little, and stood facing east;

sentences.zh: 中書令進當冊案前，讀冊訖，俯伏，興，又搢笏，奉冊於褥，東向冊函，北向進跪置御坐前，與舉冊官降還侍立位，太尉亦降，納舄、帶劍。

translations.literal: The Director of the Secretariat advanced before the patent table, finished reading the patent, prostrated himself, rose, again inserted his tablet, presented the patent on the mat, faced east to enclose it in the case, advanced facing north, knelt and placed it before the imperial throne, and with the patent-bearer descended and returned to the standing position; the Grand Commandant also descended, put on shoes, and girded on his sword.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of the Secretariat advanced to the patent table, read the patent, prostrated himself, rose, inserted his tablet again, placed the patent on the mat, enclosed it in its case facing east, then advanced facing north, knelt, and set it before the imperial throne. He and the patent-bearer descended and returned to their standing positions; the Grand Commandant also descended, put on his shoes, and girded on his sword.

sentences.zh: 禮部侍郎押寶案 升，司徒隨升，北面跪置，侍中讀寶訖，置冊之南，俱復位，其納舄、帶劍、俯伏，一如上儀。

translations.literal: The vice minister of Rites escorted the seal table up; the Minister of Education ascended with it; facing north they knelt and placed it; the Palace Attendant finished reading the seal and placed it south of the patent; all returned to position; putting on shoes, girding sword, and prostrating followed the ceremony above.
translations.idiomatic: The vice minister of Rites escorted the seal table up, with the Minister of Education following. They faced north, knelt, and set it down. The Palace Attendant read the seal and placed it south of the patent. All returned to their positions; putting on shoes, girding the sword, and prostrating followed the same procedure as above.

sentences.zh: 典儀讚在位官皆再拜，禮直官、通事舍人引太尉至西階下，解劍、舄 升，當御坐前跪賀，

translations.literal: The master of ceremonies praised all officials in attendance to bow twice; ritual officers and Communications Chamberlains led the Grand Commandant to below the western steps; he removed sword and shoes, ascended, and knelt before the imperial throne to offer congratulations,
translations.idiomatic: The master of ceremonies directed all officials present to bow twice. Ritual officers and Communications Chamberlains led the Grand Commandant to the foot of the western steps. He removed his sword and shoes, ascended, and knelt before the imperial throne to offer congratulations,

sentences.zh: 〈（其詞中書門下撰。）〉

translations.literal: (The text was drafted by the Secretariat and Chancellery.)
translations.idiomatic: (The congratulatory text was drafted by the Secretariat and Chancellery.)

sentences.zh: 賀訖復位，皆再拜，如讀冊寶儀。

translations.literal: When congratulations were finished he returned to position; all bowed twice, as in the ceremony for reading the patent and seal.
translations.idiomatic: When the congratulations were finished he returned to his position. All bowed twice, following the procedure for reading the patent and seal.

sentences.zh: 侍中升至御坐前承旨，退，臨階西向稱“有制”，典儀讚再拜訖，宣曰：“朕以鴻儀昭 舉，保命會昌，迫於群情，祗膺顯號。

translations.literal: The Palace Attendant ascended before the imperial throne to receive the edict, withdrew, stood at the steps facing west and announced "There is an edict"; when the master of ceremonies had praised the bowing twice, he proclaimed: "I, because the great ceremony was brilliantly raised, received the mandate to preserve life and bring prosperity, compelled by the feelings of the multitude, reverently accepted the illustrious title.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Attendant ascended before the throne to receive the edict, withdrew, and standing at the steps facing west announced, "His Majesty has decreed." After the master of ceremonies directed the officials to bow twice, he proclaimed: "Because the great ceremony has been brilliantly performed and the mandate to preserve life and bring prosperity received, compelled by the feelings of the multitude, I reverently accept this illustrious title.

sentences.zh: 退循寡昧，惕懼增深。

translations.literal: Reflecting on my few merits and much obscurity, my vigilance and fear grow ever deeper.
translations.idiomatic: Reflecting on my limited merit and much obscurity, my vigilance and fear grow ever deeper.

sentences.zh: 所賀知。”

translations.literal: Your congratulations are noted."
translations.idiomatic: I acknowledge your congratulations."

sentences.zh: 宣訖復位，典儀讚再拜舞蹈，三稱萬歲，又再拜訖。

translations.literal: When the proclamation was finished he returned to position; the master of ceremonies praised bowing twice and the dance, thrice shouting "Ten thousand years!," and bowing twice again.
translations.idiomatic: When the proclamation ended he returned to his position. The master of ceremonies directed the officials to bow twice and perform the dance, shout "Long live the emperor!" three times, and bow twice again.

sentences.zh: 侍中升階奏禮畢，降復位，扇上，樂 作，帝降坐，禦輿入自東房，扇開，樂止。

translations.literal: The Palace Attendant ascended the steps and reported that the rites were complete, descended and returned to position; the fans were raised, music sounded, the emperor descended from the throne, entered by imperial carriage from the east chamber, the fans were opened, and the music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Attendant ascended the steps and reported that the rites were complete, then descended and returned to his position. The fans were raised and music sounded. The emperor left the throne and entered by imperial carriage from the east chamber; when the fans were opened the music ceased.

sentences.zh: 侍中版奏解嚴，中書侍郎帥奉案官升殿，跪奉冊置於案，次門下侍郎奉寶如奉冊禮，通事舍人讚引詣東上閣門狀進，所司 承旨放仗，百官再拜訖，退如常儀。

translations.literal: The Palace Attendant reported on the placard that the vigil was dismissed; the vice chancellor of the Secretariat led the table-offering officers up the hall, knelt and presented the patent on the table; next the vice chancellor of the Chancellery presented the seal as in presenting the patent; Communications Chamberlains praised and led them to the Eastern Upper Gatehouse to submit a report for entry; the relevant offices received the order and dismissed the guard of honor; when the officials had bowed twice, they withdrew as in usual ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Attendant reported on the placard that the vigil was dismissed. The vice chancellor of the Secretariat led the table-offering officers up the hall, knelt, and placed the patent on the table. Next the vice chancellor of the Chancellery presented the seal in the same manner as the patent. Communications Chamberlains directed them to the Eastern Upper Gatehouse to submit the entry report. On imperial order the guard of honor was dismissed. After the officials bowed twice, they withdrew in the usual manner.

sentences.zh: 自後受冊皆如之。

translations.literal: From then on, receiving the patent was always like this.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, receipt of the patent always followed this procedure.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，賜百官食於朝堂。

translations.literal: When the rites were complete, food was bestowed on the officials in the court hall.
translations.idiomatic: When the rites were complete, the officials were given a meal in the court hall.

sentences.zh: 熙寧元年，宰臣曾公亮等上表請加尊號，詔不允。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xining, chief ministers Zeng Gongliang and others submitted a memorial requesting an additional honorific title; an edict did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: In Xining 1, 1068, Chief Minister Zeng Gongliang and others submitted a memorial requesting an additional honorific title; an edict refused.

sentences.zh: 先是，翰林學士司馬 光言：“尊號起唐武後、中宗之世，遂為故事。

translations.literal: Earlier, Hanlin academician Sima Guang had said: "Honorific titles began in the eras of Empress Wu and Emperor Zhongzong of Tang, and thereafter became precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Hanlin Academician Sima Guang had written: "Honorific titles began in the reigns of Empress Wu and Emperor Zhongzong of Tang and thereafter became precedent.

sentences.zh: 先帝治平二年，辭尊號不受，天下莫不稱頌聖德。

translations.literal: The late emperor in the second year of Zhiping declined the honorific title and did not accept it; throughout the realm none failed to praise his sagely virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor in Zhiping 2, 1065, declined an honorific title, and the whole realm praised his sagely virtue.

sentences.zh: 其後佞臣建言，國家與契丹常有往來書，彼有尊號而中國獨無，足 為深恥。

translations.literal: Afterward sycophantic ministers offered advice that the state and the Khitan often exchanged letters, that they had honorific titles while China alone had none—sufficient to be a deep shame.
translations.idiomatic: Later, sycophantic ministers argued that because the court and the Khitan regularly exchanged letters, and they bore honorific titles while China alone did not, this was a profound disgrace.

sentences.zh: 於是群臣復以非時上尊號，論者甚為朝廷惜之。

translations.literal: Thereupon the ministers again requested an honorific title at an inopportune time; commentators greatly regretted it for the court.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers then again requested an honorific title at an inopportune time, which commentators deeply regretted on the court's behalf.

sentences.zh: 今群臣以故事上尊號，臣愚以為陛下聰明睿知，雖宜享有鴻名，然踐祚未久，又在亮陰之中，考之事體，似 未宜受。

translations.literal: Now the ministers request an honorific title by precedent; this subject is foolish and considers that Your Majesty is intelligent and wise and, though you ought to bear a great name, yet you have not long been on the throne and are moreover in the period of bright mourning; considering the circumstances of the matter, it seems not yet appropriate to accept.
translations.idiomatic: Now the ministers are requesting an honorific title by precedent. Your servant is foolish enough to think that although Your Majesty's intelligence and wisdom certainly merit a great name, you have not long been on the throne and are still in mourning; considering the circumstances, it seems premature to accept.

sentences.zh: 陛下誠能斷以聖意，推而不居，仍令更不得上表請，則頌歎之聲將洋溢四海矣。”

translations.literal: If Your Majesty can truly decide by sagely intent, decline and not occupy it, and moreover order that no further memorials requesting it be submitted, then sounds of praise will overflow the four seas."
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty can decide by your own sagely judgment, decline the title, and order that no further memorials be submitted, praise will resound throughout the realm."

sentences.zh: 詔賜光曰：“覽卿來奏，深諒忠誠。

translations.literal: An edict bestowed on Guang said: "Having read your submitted memorial, I deeply appreciate your loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: An edict to Guang read: "Having read your memorial, I deeply appreciate your loyalty.

sentences.zh: 朕方以頻日淫雨，甲申地震，天威彰 著，日虞傾禍。

translations.literal: I am just now facing days of incessant heavy rain and an earthquake on the jiashen day; Heaven's majesty is clearly manifest, and daily I fear impending disaster.
translations.idiomatic: I am facing days of incessant heavy rain and an earthquake on the jiashen day; Heaven's majesty is clearly manifest, and I daily fear impending disaster.

sentences.zh: 被此鴻名，有慚面目，況在亮陰，亦難當是盛典。

translations.literal: To bear this great name shames my face; moreover, while in bright mourning, it is also difficult to undertake such a grand ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: To bear this great name would shame me; moreover, while in mourning it would be difficult to undertake such a grand ceremony.

sentences.zh: 今已批降指揮，可善為答辭，使中外知朕至誠慚懼，非欺眾邀名。”

translations.literal: I have now issued and transmitted orders; you may craft a good reply so that within and without all know my utmost sincerity, shame, and fear, and that I am not deceiving the multitude to seek a name."
translations.idiomatic: I have now issued orders. Craft an appropriate reply so that court and country alike know my sincere shame and fear, and that I am not deceiving the people to win renown."

sentences.zh: 其後，宰臣數上表請，終不 允。

translations.literal: Afterward the chief ministers several times submitted memorials requesting it, but in the end it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the chief ministers submitted several more memorials, but in the end the request was never granted.

sentences.zh: 徽宗內禪，欽宗上尊號曰教主道君太上皇帝，居龍德宮。

translations.literal: Huizong abdicated; Qinzong conferred the honorific title Supreme Emperor, Lord Who Teaches the Way, and he resided at Longde Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Huizong abdicated, Qinzong conferred on him the honorific title Supreme Emperor, Lord Who Teaches the Way, and he took up residence at Longde Palace.

sentences.zh: 靖康元年正月朔，朝賀畢，車駕詣龍德宮賀，百官班門外，宰執進見如儀。

translations.literal: On the first day of the first month of the first year of Jingkang, when the court congratulations were finished, the imperial carriage went to Longde Palace to offer congratulations; the hundred officials formed ranks outside the gate; chief ministers entered audience according to ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day of Jingkang 1, 1126, after the court congratulations were finished, the imperial carriage proceeded to Longde Palace to offer congratulations. Officials formed ranks outside the gate, and the chief ministers entered audience according to ceremony.

sentences.zh: 高宗內禪。

translations.literal: Gaozong's abdication.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong's Abdication.

sentences.zh: 紹興三十二年六月十日禦劄：“皇太子可即皇帝位，朕稱太上皇帝，退處德壽宮，皇后稱太上皇后。

translations.literal: On the tenth day of the sixth month of the thirty-second year of Shaoxing, an imperial note: "The crown prince may immediately take the emperor's throne; I shall be styled Supreme Emperor and retire to Deshou Palace; the empress shall be styled Supreme Empress.
translations.idiomatic: On the tenth day of the sixth month of Shaoxing 32, 1162, an imperial note read: "The crown prince may immediately ascend the throne. I shall be styled Supreme Emperor and retire to Deshou Palace; the empress shall be styled Supreme Empress.

sentences.zh: 應軍國事並聽嗣君處分。”

translations.literal: All military and state affairs shall be left to the disposition of the succeeding ruler.
translations.idiomatic: All military and state affairs shall be left to the disposition of the succeeding ruler.

sentences.zh: 十一日，行內禪之禮。

translations.literal: On the eleventh day, the ceremony of inner abdication was performed.
translations.idiomatic: On the eleventh day the inner-abdication ceremony was performed.

sentences.zh: 有司設仗紫宸殿，宰臣、文武百僚立班，皇帝出宮，鳴鞭，禁衛諸班直、親從儀仗並內侍省執骨朵使臣等並迎駕，自讚常起居。

translations.literal: The relevant offices set up the guard of honor at Zichen Hall; chief ministers and civil and military officials of the hundred ranks stood in formation; the emperor left the palace; the whip was sounded; all guard units on duty, personal attendants' guard of honor, and Inner Service attendants bearing maces all welcomed the imperial progress, praising themselves in the usual health report.
translations.idiomatic: The relevant offices set up the guard of honor at Zichen Hall. Chief ministers and all civil and military officials formed ranks. The emperor left the palace to the crack of the whip. Palace guards on duty, the personal attendants' escort, and Inner Service attendants bearing maces all welcomed the imperial progress with the usual health report.

sentences.zh: 皇帝升禦 坐，知閣門官以下並內侍都知、禦帶以下一班起居，次管軍一班起居，次宰執以下常起居訖，左仆射陳康伯、知樞密院事葉義問、參知政事汪澈、同知樞密院事黃祖 舜升殿奏曰：“臣等不才，輔政累年，罪戾山積，乃蒙容貸，不賜誅責。

translations.literal: The emperor ascended the imperial throne; the Director of the Gatehouse and below, together with the Director of the Inner Service, Imperial Girdle Attendants and below, reported health in one rank; next the commanders of the guard reported health in one rank; next after the chief ministers had reported health as usual, Left Vice Director Chen Kangbo, Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs Ye Yiwen, Vice Director of the Secretariat Wang Che, and Associate Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs Huang Zushun ascended the hall and memorialized: "We subjects are without talent; we have assisted in government for many years; our offenses are piled like mountains; yet we have been granted tolerance and not given execution or punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ascended the throne. The Director of the Gatehouse and below, together with the Director of the Inner Service and Imperial Girdle Attendants, reported on the emperor's health in one rank; next the commanders of the guard did so; then the chief ministers reported as usual. Left Vice Director Chen Kangbo, Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs Ye Yiwen, Vice Director of the Secretariat Wang Che, and Associate Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs Huang Zushun ascended the hall and said: "We are without talent and have assisted in government for many years. Our offenses are piled like mountains, yet we have been spared execution or punishment.

sentences.zh: 今陛下超然獨斷，高蹈堯、舜之舉，臣等心實欽仰。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty has transcendentally decided alone, loftily treading the deeds of Yao and Shun; in our hearts we truly admire and look up.
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty has acted with transcendent resolve, loftily following the example of Yao and Shun, and we are filled with admiration.

sentences.zh: 但自此不獲日望清光，犬馬之情，不勝 依戀。”

translations.literal: But from now on we shall not daily behold your clear radiance; our feelings as hounds and horses cannot overcome our attachment."
translations.idiomatic: But from now on we shall no longer daily behold your presence, and our devotion as your humble servants cannot overcome our attachment."

sentences.zh: 因再拜辭，相與泣下，幾至號慟。

translations.literal: Thereupon they bowed twice in farewell; together they wept, nearly to wailing and anguish.
translations.idiomatic: They bowed twice in farewell, wept together, and were nearly overcome with grief.

sentences.zh: 帝亦為之流涕曰：“朕在位三十六年，今老且病，久欲閑退，此事斷自朕心，非由臣下開陳，卿等當悉力以輔嗣君。”

translations.literal: The emperor also wept for them and said: "I have been on the throne thirty-six years; now I am old and ill and have long wished to retire; this matter was decided by my own heart and was not opened and presented by subjects below; you should all exert your strength to assist the succeeding ruler."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wept as well and said: "I have reigned thirty-six years. I am old and ill and have long wished to retire. This decision came from my own heart, not from my ministers. You must all devote yourselves to assisting the new emperor."

sentences.zh: 康 伯等復奏曰：“皇太子仁聖，天下所共知，似聞謙遜太過，未肯便禦正殿。”

translations.literal: Kangbo and the others again memorialized: "The crown prince is benevolent and sagely, known throughout the realm; it seems we hear he is overly modest and humble and is not yet willing immediately to proceed to the main hall."
translations.idiomatic: Kangbo and the others added: "The crown prince's benevolence and sagacity are known throughout the realm, but we hear he is excessively modest and has not yet been willing to take the main throne."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：“朕前此固嚐與之言，早來禁中又麵諭之，即步行徑趨側殿門，欲還東宮，已再 三敦勉邀留，今在殿後矣。”

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I had already spoken with him on this before; early this morning in the inner palace I also instructed him face to face; he immediately walked straight to the side hall gate, wishing to return to the Eastern Palace; I have already urged and detained him two or three times; he is now behind the hall."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "I had already spoken with him about this. Early this morning in the inner palace I instructed him again in person. He immediately walked straight to the side hall gate, intending to return to the Eastern Palace. I have urged and detained him two or three times; he is now behind the hall."

sentences.zh: 宰執降階，皇帝降坐，鳴鞭還內。

translations.literal: The chief ministers descended the steps; the emperor descended from the throne; the whip was sounded and he returned within.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers descended the steps. The emperor left the throne, the whip was sounded, and he returned to the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 宰臣文武百僚並退，立班，聽宣詔訖，再拜舞蹈，三稱萬歲，再拜訖，班權退，復追班入，詣殿下立 班。

translations.literal: Chief ministers and civil and military officials of the hundred ranks all withdrew, stood in formation, listened until the edict was proclaimed, bowed twice and performed the dance, thrice shouted "Ten thousand years!," bowed twice again; the ranks temporarily withdrew, then were called back in formation, proceeded to below the hall and stood in ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Chief ministers and all civil and military officials withdrew and formed ranks. After the edict was proclaimed they bowed twice, performed the dance, shouted "Long live the emperor!" three times, and bowed twice again. The ranks temporarily withdrew, then were called back in and took their places below the hall.

sentences.zh: 少頃，新皇帝服履袍，涕泣出宮。

translations.literal: After a short while, the new emperor, wearing court robes, weeping came forth from the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward the new emperor, wearing court robes, emerged from the palace in tears.

sentences.zh: 禁衛諸班直、親從儀仗等迎駕，起居，鳴鞭。

translations.literal: All guard units on duty, personal attendants' guard of honor, and the like welcomed the imperial progress, reported health, and sounded the whip.
translations.idiomatic: Palace guards on duty and the personal attendants' escort welcomed the imperial progress, reported on the emperor's health, and sounded the whip.

sentences.zh: 內侍扶掖皇帝至禦榻，涕泣再三，不坐，內侍傳太上皇帝聖旨，請 皇帝升御坐，皇帝升御坐東側坐。

translations.literal: Inner attendants supported the emperor to the imperial couch; he wept again and again and would not sit; inner attendants transmitted the Supreme Emperor's holy edict, requesting the emperor to ascend the imperial throne; the emperor ascended and sat on the east side of the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Inner attendants supported the emperor to the imperial couch. He wept repeatedly and would not sit. Inner attendants conveyed the Supreme Emperor's edict requesting that he ascend the throne. The emperor ascended and sat on the east side of the throne.

sentences.zh: 知閣門官以下一班起居、稱賀，次管軍官一班起居、稱賀，次文武百僚橫行北向立，舍人當殿稱文武百僚宰臣陳康伯以下起居、稱 賀，皇帝降御坐，側身西向不坐。

translations.literal: The Director of the Gatehouse and below reported health and offered congratulations in one rank; next the commanders of the guard reported health and offered congratulations in one rank; next civil and military officials of the hundred ranks stood transversely facing north; the Chamberlain before the hall announced civil and military officials, chief ministers Chen Kangbo and below, reporting health and offering congratulations; the emperor descended from the throne and, turning aside, faced west and did not sit.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of the Gatehouse and below reported on the emperor's health and offered congratulations in one rank; next the commanders of the guard did the same; then civil and military officials stood in transverse ranks facing north. The Chamberlain announced that civil and military officials, including Chief Minister Chen Kangbo and below, were reporting on the emperor's health and offering congratulations. The emperor left the throne, turned aside facing west, and did not sit.

sentences.zh: 俟宰臣以下再拜舞蹈、三稱萬歲、起居、稱賀畢，康伯等升殿奏：“臣等言：願陛下即御坐，以正南面，上副太上皇帝傳授之意。”

translations.literal: When the chief ministers and below had finished bowing twice, performing the dance, thrice shouting "Ten thousand years!," reporting health, and offering congratulations, Kangbo and the others ascended the hall and memorialized: "We subjects say: We wish Your Majesty immediately to take the imperial throne, to face due south correctly, above matching the Supreme Emperor's intent in transmitting the succession."
translations.idiomatic: When the chief ministers and others had finished bowing twice, performing the dance, shouting "Long live the emperor!" three times, reporting on his health, and offering congratulations, Kangbo and the others ascended the hall and said: "We beg Your Majesty to take the throne at once and face due south, in fulfillment of the Supreme Emperor's intent in passing on the succession."

sentences.zh: 帝愀然曰：“君父之命出於獨斷，此大位，懼不敢當，尚容辭避。”

translations.literal: The emperor, with a sorrowful countenance, said: "The command of father and ruler issued from his independent decision; this great position—I fear I dare not undertake it and still ask to be allowed to decline and avoid it."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, with a sorrowful expression, said: "My father and sovereign decided this on his own. This great position—I fear I dare not accept it and must still ask to decline."

sentences.zh: 康伯等再奏：“茲者伏遇皇帝陛下應天順人，龍飛寶位，第以駑下之材，恐不足以仰輔新政， 然依乘風雲千載之遇，實與四海蒼生不勝幸慶。”

translations.literal: Kangbo and the others again memorialized: "Now we humbly encounter Your Majesty responding to Heaven and following the people, the dragon soaring to the precious throne; only with our inferior talents we fear we are not sufficient to look up and assist the new government; yet relying on riding wind and clouds in a thousand-year encounter, truly with the black-haired people of the four seas we cannot overcome our fortunate rejoicing."
translations.idiomatic: Kangbo and the others added: "We humbly encounter Your Majesty responding to Heaven and following the people, ascending the throne like a dragon soaring aloft. With our meager talents we fear we may not suffice to assist the new government, yet to ride the winds of this once-in-a-millennium moment is a fortune beyond measure for all the people under Heaven."

sentences.zh: 再拜賀畢，奏事而退。

translations.literal: When they had bowed twice and finished congratulations, they memorialized on affairs and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: After bowing twice and finishing their congratulations, they presented their business and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 宰執下殿，皇帝還內，鳴鞭。

translations.literal: The chief ministers descended from the hall; the emperor returned within; the whip was sounded.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers left the hall. The emperor returned to the inner palace to the crack of the whip.

sentences.zh: 宰執文武百僚赴祥曦殿，候太上皇帝登輦，扈從至德壽宮而 退。

translations.literal: Chief ministers and civil and military officials of the hundred ranks went to Xiangxi Hall, waited for the Supreme Emperor to mount the carriage, escorted him to Deshou Palace, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Chief ministers and all civil and military officials went to Xiangxi Hall, waited for the Supreme Emperor to mount his carriage, escorted him to Deshou Palace, and then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 翌日，詣德壽宮朝見。

translations.literal: The next day, he proceeded to Deshou Palace for the court audience.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he proceeded to Deshou Palace for an audience.

sentences.zh: 前期，儀鸞司設大次於德壽宮門內，小次於殿東廊西向。

translations.literal: Beforehand, the Directorate of Ceremonial Insignia set up the great resting place inside the gate of Deshou Palace and the small resting place in the eastern corridor of the hall, facing west.
translations.idiomatic: In advance, the Directorate of Ceremonial Insignia set up the great resting pavilion inside the gate of Deshou Palace and the small resting pavilion in the eastern corridor of the hall, facing west.

sentences.zh: 其日，俟皇帝出即御坐，從駕臣僚、禁衛等起居如常儀。

translations.literal: On that day, when the emperor came forth he immediately took the throne; accompanying officials, guards, and the like reported health as in usual ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: On that day, when the emperor emerged he immediately took the throne. Accompanying officials and guards reported on his health in the usual manner.

sentences.zh: 皇帝降禦 坐，乘輦至德壽宮，文武百僚詣宮門外迎駕，起居訖，前導官、太常卿、閣門官、太常博士、禮直官先入，詣大次前，分左右立定，俟皇帝降輦入，次御史台、閣 門、太常寺報文武百僚入，詣殿庭北向立定。

translations.literal: The emperor descended from the throne, rode the carriage to Deshou Palace; civil and military officials of the hundred ranks went outside the palace gate to welcome the imperial progress; when health was reported, advance officers, the Minister of Rites, gate officers, Doctors of Rites, and ritual officers entered first, proceeded before the great resting place, stood fixed to left and right, waited for the emperor to descend from the carriage and enter; next the Censorate, Gatehouse, and Temple of Rites announced the entry of civil and military officials of the hundred ranks, who proceeded to the hall courtyard and stood fixed facing north.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor left the throne and rode in his carriage to Deshou Palace. Civil and military officials went outside the palace gate to welcome him. After the health report, advance officers, the Minister of Rites, gate officers, Doctors of Rites, and ritual officers entered first and took their places to the left and right before the great resting pavilion, waiting for the emperor to dismount and enter. Next the Censorate, Gatehouse, and Temple of Rites announced the entry of all officials, who proceeded to the hall courtyard and stood facing north.

sentences.zh: 前導官導皇帝入小次，簾降，俟太上皇帝即御坐，小次簾卷，前導官導皇帝升殿東階，詣殿上折檻前，奏請拜，皇帝再 拜訖，前導官導皇帝稍前，躬奏聖躬萬福訖，復位，再拜訖，導皇帝詣太上皇帝御坐之東，西向立。

translations.literal: Advance officers led the emperor into the small resting place; the curtain was lowered; when the Supreme Emperor had taken the throne, the curtain of the small resting place was raised; advance officers led the emperor up the eastern steps of the hall, proceeded before the folding balustrade on the hall, memorialized requesting a bow; when the emperor had bowed twice, advance officers led the emperor slightly forward, bowed and memorialized on the sage body's ten thousand blessings; when finished he returned to position, bowed twice again; they led the emperor to the east of the Supreme Emperor's throne and he stood facing west.
translations.idiomatic: Advance officers led the emperor into the small resting pavilion and lowered the curtain. When the Supreme Emperor had taken the throne, the curtain was raised. Advance officers led the emperor up the eastern steps to before the folding balustrade and requested that he bow. After the emperor bowed twice, they led him slightly forward to report on the Supreme Emperor's health, then led him back to bow twice again, and finally to stand west of the Supreme Emperor's throne, facing west.

sentences.zh: 殿下在位官皆再拜，搢笏，三舞蹈，三叩頭，出笏就拜，又再 拜，班首不離位，奏聖躬萬福，又再拜，班退，前導官以次退，從駕官歸幕次，以俟從駕。

translations.literal: All officials in attendance below the hall bowed twice, inserted their tablets, performed the dance three times, knocked the head three times, withdrew the tablets and completed the bow, bowed twice again; the head of the rank did not leave position, memorialized on the sage body's ten thousand blessings, bowed twice again; the ranks withdrew; advance officers withdrew in order; accompanying officials returned to the tent quarters to await accompanying the imperial progress.
translations.idiomatic: All officials below the hall bowed twice, inserted their tablets, performed the dance three times and kowtowed three times, withdrew their tablets and completed the bow, then bowed twice again. The head of the rank, without leaving his place, reported on the Supreme Emperor's health and bowed twice more. The ranks withdrew; advance officers withdrew in order; accompanying officials returned to the tent quarters to await the imperial departure.

sentences.zh: 太上皇帝駕興，皇帝從，入見太上皇后，如宮中之儀。

translations.literal: When the Supreme Emperor's carriage rose, the emperor followed; he entered to see the Supreme Empress according to inner-palace ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: When the Supreme Emperor's carriage set out, the emperor followed and entered to see the Supreme Empress according to inner-palace ceremony.

sentences.zh: 皇帝還內，如來 儀。

translations.literal: The emperor returned within, as on the way coming.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor returned to the inner palace by the same route.

sentences.zh: 每遇正旦、冬至及朔望，並依上儀。

translations.literal: Whenever encountering New Year's Day, the winter solstice, and the new and full moons, all followed the ceremony above.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day, the winter solstice, and the new and full moons, the same procedure was followed.

sentences.zh: 十二日，帝詣德壽宮，以雨，百僚免入見，上就宮中行禮。

translations.literal: On the twelfth day, the emperor proceeded to Deshou Palace; because of rain, the hundred officials were excused from entering for audience; the emperor above performed the rites within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On the twelfth day the emperor proceeded to Deshou Palace. Because of rain, officials were excused from entering, and the emperor performed the rites within the palace.

sentences.zh: 自後詣宮，若行宮中禮，即不集百官陪位。

translations.literal: From then on, when proceeding to the palace, if performing inner-palace rites, the hundred officials were not assembled to attend in place.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, when the emperor went to the palace to perform inner-palace rites, officials were not assembled to attend.

sentences.zh: 十三 日，詔令宰臣率百官於初二日、十六日詣德壽宮起居。

translations.literal: On the thirteenth day, an edict ordered chief ministers to lead the hundred officials on the second and sixteenth days of each month to proceed to Deshou Palace to report on health.
translations.idiomatic: On the thirteenth day an edict ordered the chief ministers to lead all officials to Deshou Palace on the second and sixteenth of each month to report on the Supreme Emperor's health.

sentences.zh: 又詔：“朕欲每日一朝德壽宮，修晨昏之禮。

translations.literal: Another edict said: "I wish daily to hold court once at Deshou Palace and observe the rites of morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict read: "I wish to visit Deshou Palace every day and observe the rites of morning and evening attendance.

sentences.zh: 麵奉慈訓，恐廢萬機，勞煩群下，不蒙賜許。

translations.literal: To receive kind instruction face to face—I fear neglecting the myriad affairs, troubling and wearying the multitude below—and this was not granted permission.
translations.idiomatic: To receive my father's instruction in person would, I fear, neglect the myriad affairs of state and burden my ministers, and this was not permitted.

sentences.zh: 禮官宜重定其期， 如前代朝朔望，甚為疏闊，朕不敢取。”

translations.literal: Ritual officers should redetermine the schedule; as in former dynasties attending on the new and full moons—it is very lax and broad, and I dare not adopt it."
translations.idiomatic: The ritual officers should set a new schedule. The practice of former dynasties, attending only on the new and full moons, is far too infrequent, and I dare not adopt it."

sentences.zh: 於是禮部、太常寺言：“《漢書》高皇帝五日一朝太上皇，乞依此故事，每五日一次詣德壽宮朝見，如宮中禮。”

translations.literal: Thereupon the Ministry of Rites and the Temple of Rites said: "The 《Book of Han》 records that the High Emperor attended the Supreme Emperor once every five days; we request following this precedent, once every five days proceeding to Deshou Palace for audience, as in inner-palace ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites and the Temple of Rites then reported: "The 《Book of Han》 records that Emperor Gaozu of Han attended the Supreme Emperor once every five days. We request following this precedent and visiting Deshou Palace once every five days, using inner-palace ceremony.

sentences.zh: 帝始禦後殿，宰臣陳康伯等奏：“臣等朝德壽宮，太上皇宣諭，車駕每至宮，必於門外降輦，已再三勉諭，既行家人之禮，自宜至殿上降輦。”

translations.literal: When the emperor first proceeded to the rear hall, chief ministers Chen Kangbo and others memorialized: "We subjects attended at Deshou Palace; the Supreme Emperor proclaimed and instructed that whenever the imperial carriage arrived at the palace it must descend from the carriage outside the gate; he has already urged this two or three times; since family rites are being performed, it is fitting naturally to descend from the carriage at the hall."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor first proceeded to the rear hall, Chief Minister Chen Kangbo and others reported: "When we attended at Deshou Palace, the Supreme Emperor instructed that whenever Your Majesty's carriage arrives at the palace you must dismount outside the gate. He has urged this repeatedly. Since this is a family rite, you should naturally dismount at the hall."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：“太上有旨 不須五日一朝，隻朝朔望，朕心未安，宜令有司詳議。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The Supreme One has issued instructions that attendance every five days is not required, only on the new and full moons; my heart is not at ease; the relevant offices should deliberate in detail.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "The Supreme Emperor has instructed that attendance every five days is not required and that visits should be limited to the new and full moons. I am not at ease with this and order the relevant offices to deliberate further.

sentences.zh: 如宮門降輦，臣子禮所當然。”

translations.literal: As for descending from the carriage at the palace gate, that is what subject-ritual ought naturally to be."
translations.idiomatic: Dismounting at the palace gate is what a subject's ritual propriety requires."

sentences.zh: 於是禮部、太常言：“除朝朔望外，乞於每月初八、二十三日詣德壽宮起居， 如宮中儀。”

translations.literal: Thereupon the Ministry of Rites and the Temple of Rites said: "Apart from attending on the new and full moons, we request on the eighth and twenty-third days of each month proceeding to Deshou Palace to report on health, as in inner-palace ceremony."
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites and the Temple of Rites then proposed: "Apart from attendance on the new and full moons, we request visits to Deshou Palace on the eighth and twenty-third of each month to report on the Supreme Emperor's health, using inner-palace ceremony."

sentences.zh: 自後皆遵此製，如值雨、盛暑、祁寒，臨期承太上特旨乃免。

translations.literal: From then on all followed this regulation; if encountering rain, extreme heat, or severe cold, only on receiving a special edict from the Supreme One at the appointed time was it excused.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter this regulation was followed. Visits were excused only when rain, extreme heat, or severe cold intervened and the Supreme Emperor issued a special edict on the appointed day.

sentences.zh: 十一月冬至，上詣德壽宮稱賀上壽，禮畢，入見太后，如宮中禮。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month at the winter solstice, the emperor proceeded to Deshou Palace to offer congratulations and wish long life; when the rites were complete, he entered to see the empress dowager as in inner-palace ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: On the winter solstice in the eleventh month the emperor proceeded to Deshou Palace to offer congratulations and wish the Supreme Emperor long life. When the rites were complete, he entered to see the empress dowager according to inner-palace ceremony.

sentences.zh: 自後冬至並同。

translations.literal: From then on the winter solstice was always the same.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the winter solstice was always observed in the same way.

sentences.zh: 隆興元年正月朔，帝率百官詣德壽宮，如冬至儀。

translations.literal: On the first day of the first month of the first year of Longxing, the emperor led the hundred officials to Deshou Palace, as in the winter solstice ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day of Longxing 1, 1163, the emperor led all officials to Deshou Palace, following the winter solstice ceremony.

sentences.zh: 自後正旦並同。

translations.literal: From then on New Year's Day was always the same.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter New Year's Day was always observed in the same way.

sentences.zh: 淳熙十六年，孝宗內禪，皇太子即皇帝位；

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Chunxi, Xiaozong abdicated; the crown prince immediately took the emperor's throne;
translations.idiomatic: In Chunxi 16, 1189, Xiaozong abdicated and the crown prince immediately ascended the throne;

sentences.zh: 紹熙五年，光宗內禪，皇子嘉王即皇帝位，並如紹興三十二年故事。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Shaoxi, Guangzong abdicated within the palace; the prince, Prince of Jia, immediately took the emperor's throne; all followed the precedent of the thirty-second year of Shaoxing.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoxi 5, 1194, Guangzong abdicated, and the prince, the Prince of Jia, immediately ascended the throne; everything followed the precedent of Shaoxing 32.

sentences.zh: 太皇太后、皇 太后、皇太妃冊禮。

translations.literal: The patent ceremony for the grand empress dowager, the empress dowager, and the imperial consort dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Ceremonies for patenting the grand empress dowager, empress dowager, and imperial consort dowager.

sentences.zh: 建隆元年，詔尊母南陽郡太夫人為皇太后，仍令所司追冊四親廟。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianlong, an edict honored his mother, the Grand Lady of Nanyang Commandery, as empress dowager, and still ordered the relevant offices to confer posthumous patents on the four kin temples.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianlong 1, 960, an edict honored the emperor's mother, Lady Nanyang, as empress dowager and ordered the relevant offices to confer posthumous patents at the four kin temples.

sentences.zh: 後不果行。

translations.literal: Later it was not carried through.
translations.idiomatic: In the end this was not carried out.

sentences.zh: 至道三年四月，尊太宗皇后李氏為皇太后，宰臣等詣崇政殿門表賀 皇帝，又詣內東門表賀皇太后。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the third year of Zhidao, Empress Li, consort of Taizong, was honored as empress dowager; chief ministers and others proceeded to the gate of Chongzheng Hall and presented memorials of congratulation to the emperor, and again proceeded to the Inner Eastern Gate and presented memorials of congratulation to the empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Zhidao 3, 997, Empress Li, consort of Emperor Taizong, was honored as empress dowager. Chief ministers went to the gate of Chongzheng Hall to submit congratulatory memorials to the emperor, then to the Inner Eastern Gate to submit congratulatory memorials to the empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 乾興元年，真宗遺製尊皇后劉氏為皇太后，淑妃楊氏為皇太妃，亦不果行冊禮。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianxing, by Zhenzong's testamentary instructions Empress Liu was honored as empress dowager and Pure Consort Yang as imperial consort dowager; the patent ceremony likewise was not carried through.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianxing 1, 1022, by Zhenzong's testamentary instructions Empress Liu was honored as empress dowager and Pure Consort Yang as imperial consort dowager, but the patent ceremony was likewise not performed.

sentences.zh: 天聖二年，宰臣王欽若等五表請上皇太 後尊號。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tiansheng, chief ministers Wang Qinruo and others five times submitted memorials requesting that an honorific title be conferred on the empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiansheng 2, 1024, Chief Minister Wang Qinruo and others submitted five memorials requesting an honorific title for the empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 十一月，郊祀畢，帝御天安殿受冊，百官稱賀畢，再序班。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, when the suburban sacrifice was completed, the emperor proceeded to Tian'an Hall to receive the patent; when the hundred officials had finished offering congratulations, ranks were re-formed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, after the suburban sacrifice was completed, the emperor proceeded to Tian'an Hall to receive the patent. After officials had offered congratulations, the ranks were re-formed.

sentences.zh: 侍中奏中嚴外辦，禮儀使奏發冊寶，帝服通天冠、絳紗袍，秉珪以出。

translations.literal: The Palace Attendant memorialized that inner strictness and outer preparation were complete; the commissioner of ceremonial propriety memorialized to issue the patent and seal; the emperor, wearing the Tongtian cap and crimson gauze robe, holding the jade tablet, came forth.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Attendant announced that inner strictness and outer preparation were complete. The commissioner of ceremonial propriety announced the issuance of the patent and seal. The emperor, wearing the Tongtian cap and crimson gauze robe and holding the jade tablet, came forth.

sentences.zh: 禮儀使、閣門使導帝隨冊 寶降自西階，內臣奉至殿庭，置橫街南東向褥位，冊在北，寶在南，帝立殿庭北向褥位，奉冊寶官奉冊寶案，太常卿、吏部、禮部侍郎引置當中褥位。

translations.literal: The commissioner of ceremonial propriety and the director of the gatehouse guided the emperor, following the patent and seal, down the western steps; inner attendants carried them to the hall court and placed them on the eastern-facing cushion south of the cross street, the patent to the north and the seal to the south; the emperor stood on the northern-facing cushion in the hall court; officials bearing the patent and seal carried the patent and seal table; the Director of the Temple of Rites, the Vice Minister of Personnel, and the Vice Minister of Rites led them and placed them on the central cushion.
translations.idiomatic: The commissioner of ceremonial propriety and the director of the gatehouse guided the emperor down the western steps, following the patent and seal. Inner attendants carried them to the hall court and set them on an eastern-facing cushion south of the cross street, with the patent to the north and the seal to the south. The emperor stood on a northern-facing cushion in the hall court while officials bearing the patent and seal carried the patent and seal table. The Director of the Temple of Rites and the vice ministers of Personnel and Rites led them forward and placed them on the central cushion.

sentences.zh: 禮儀使奏請皇 帝再拜，在位官皆再拜。

translations.literal: The commissioner of ceremonial propriety memorialized requesting that the emperor bow twice; all officials in attendance likewise bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: The commissioner of ceremonial propriety requested that the emperor bow twice, and all officials in attendance did likewise.

sentences.zh: 太尉、司徒就冊寶位，帝搢珪跪，奉冊授太尉，又奉寶授司徒，皆搢笏東向跪受，興，奉冊寶案置於近東西向褥位。

translations.literal: The Grand Commandant and the Minister over the Masses took their places at the patent and seal; the emperor inserted the jade tablet and knelt, presented the patent to the Grand Commandant, and again presented the seal to the Minister over the Masses; all inserted their tablets, knelt facing east to receive them, rose, and carried the patent and seal table to place it on the nearby eastern-facing cushion.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Commandant and the Minister over the Masses took their places at the patent and seal. The emperor inserted the jade tablet and knelt, presenting the patent to the Grand Commandant and then the seal to the Minister over the Masses. Both inserted their tablets and knelt facing east to receive them, then rose and carried the patent and seal table to a nearby eastern-facing cushion.

sentences.zh: 禮儀使奏請皇帝歸禦 幄，易常服，乘輿赴文德殿後幄，百官班退赴朝堂，太尉、司徒奉冊寶至文德殿外幄，太尉以下各就次以俟。

translations.literal: The commissioner of ceremonial propriety memorialized requesting that the emperor return to the imperial curtain, change into ordinary dress, and ride the imperial carriage to the rear curtain of Wende Hall; the hundred officials withdrew in ranks to the court hall; the Grand Commandant and Minister over the Masses carried the patent and seal to the outer curtain of Wende Hall; the Grand Commandant and below each took their stations to wait.
translations.idiomatic: The commissioner of ceremonial propriety requested that the emperor return to the imperial curtain, change into ordinary dress, and ride the imperial carriage to the rear curtain of Wende Hall. Officials withdrew in ranks to the court hall. The Grand Commandant and Minister over the Masses carried the patent and seal to the outer curtain of Wende Hall, and the Grand Commandant and those below each took their stations to wait.

sentences.zh: 侍中奏中嚴外辦，太后服儀天冠、袞衣以 出，奏《隆安之樂》，行障、步障、方團扇，侍衛垂簾，即御坐，南向，樂止。

translations.literal: The Palace Attendant memorialized that inner strictness and outer preparation were complete; the empress dowager, wearing the Yitian cap and ceremonial robe, came forth; the music 《Long'an》 was performed; processional screens, walking screens, and square round fans were deployed; attendants lowered the curtain; she immediately took the imperial seat facing south; the music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Attendant announced that inner strictness and outer preparation were complete. The empress dowager, wearing the Yitian cap and ceremonial robe, came forth to the music 《Long'an》. Processional screens, walking screens, and square round fans were deployed, attendants lowered the curtain, and she took the imperial seat facing south. The music then ceased.

sentences.zh: 太常卿導冊案至殿西階下，各歸班，在位者皆再拜。

translations.literal: The Director of the Temple of Rites guided the patent table to below the western steps of the hall; each returned to rank; all in attendance bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of the Temple of Rites guided the patent table to the foot of the western steps of the hall. Each official returned to rank, and all in attendance bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 太尉押冊案，司徒奉冊，中書令 讀冊訖，侍中押寶案，司徒奉寶，侍中讀寶畢，太尉、司徒詣香案前，分班東西序立。

translations.literal: The Grand Commandant escorted the patent table; the Minister over the Masses bore the patent; the Director of the Secretariat finished reading the patent; the Palace Attendant escorted the seal table; the Minister over the Masses bore the seal; the Palace Attendant finished reading the seal; the Grand Commandant and Minister over the Masses proceeded before the incense table and stood in ranks east and west.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Commandant escorted the patent table while the Minister over the Masses bore the patent, and the Director of the Secretariat read the patent. The Palace Attendant escorted the seal table while the Minister over the Masses bore the seal, and the Palace Attendant read the seal. The Grand Commandant and Minister over the Masses then proceeded to the incense table and stood in ranks to the east and west.

sentences.zh: 尚宮讚引皇帝詣皇太后坐前，帝服靴袍，簾內行稱賀禮，跪曰：“嗣皇帝臣某 言：皇太后陛下顯崇徽號，昭煥寰瀛，伏惟與天同壽，率土不勝欣抃。”

translations.literal: The Senior Lady of the Palace announced and led the emperor to before the empress dowager's seat; the emperor, wearing boots and robe, performed the congratulatory rite within the curtain, knelt, and said: "The succeeding emperor, your subject So-and-so, says: Your Majesty the Empress Dowager has prominently elevated the honorific title, brilliantly illuminating all within the seas; humbly may you share Heaven's longevity; throughout the land none can overcome their joyful exultation."
translations.idiomatic: The Senior Lady of the Palace announced and led the emperor to the empress dowager's seat. Wearing boots and robe, the emperor performed the congratulatory rite within the curtain, knelt, and said: "The succeeding emperor, your subject, reports: Your Majesty the Empress Dowager has been granted this elevated honorific title, brilliantly illuminating all within the seas. May you share Heaven's longevity; throughout the land none can contain their joy."

sentences.zh: 俯伏，興，又再拜，尚宮詣御坐承旨，退，西向稱：“皇太后答曰：皇帝孝思至誠，貫於天 地，受茲徽號，感慰良深。”

translations.literal: He prostrated himself, rose, and again bowed twice; the Senior Lady of the Palace proceeded to the imperial seat to receive instructions, withdrew, and facing west announced: "The empress dowager replies: The emperor's filial thought is utmost sincerity, penetrating Heaven and Earth; receiving this honorific title, my feeling of gratitude and consolation is truly deep."
translations.idiomatic: He prostrated himself, rose, and bowed twice again. The Senior Lady of the Palace went to the imperial seat to receive instructions, withdrew, and facing west announced: "The empress dowager replies: The emperor's filial devotion is utterly sincere and reaches through Heaven and Earth. In receiving this honorific title, my gratitude and consolation are profound."

sentences.zh: 帝再拜，尚宮引歸禦幄，太尉率百官稱賀，奏《隆安之樂》，太后降坐還幄，樂止。

translations.literal: The emperor bowed twice; the Senior Lady of the Palace led him back to the imperial curtain; the Grand Commandant led the hundred officials in offering congratulations; the music 《Long'an》 was performed; the empress dowager descended from the seat and returned to the curtain; the music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor bowed twice. The Senior Lady of the Palace led him back to the imperial curtain. The Grand Commandant led all officials in offering congratulations to the music 《Long'an》. The empress dowager left the seat and returned to the curtain, and the music ceased.

sentences.zh: 侍中奏解嚴，所司放仗，百官再拜退。

translations.literal: The Palace Attendant memorialized the lifting of strictness; the relevant offices dismissed the guard of honor; the hundred officials bowed twice and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Attendant announced the lifting of strictness. The relevant offices dismissed the guard of honor, and officials bowed twice and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 太后還內， 內外命婦稱賀太后、皇帝於內殿，在外命婦及兩京留司官並奉表稱賀。

translations.literal: The empress dowager returned within; inner and outer titled ladies offered congratulations to the empress dowager and emperor in the inner hall; titled ladies outside and officials remaining on duty in the two capitals all presented memorials of congratulation.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager returned to the inner palace. Titled ladies within and without the palace offered congratulations to the empress dowager and emperor in the inner hall, and titled ladies outside the palace and officials remaining on duty in the two capitals all submitted congratulatory memorials.

sentences.zh: 自是，上皇太后尊號禮皆如之。

translations.literal: From this time on, ceremonies for conferring honorific titles on the empress dowager all followed this model.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, ceremonies for conferring honorific titles on the empress dowager all followed this model.

sentences.zh: 熙寧二年，神宗尊皇太后曹氏為太皇太后，詣文德殿跪奉玉冊授攝太尉曾公亮、金寶授攝司徒韓絳，又跪奉皇太后高氏玉冊授攝太尉文彥博、金寶授攝司徒趙抃，禮畢，百官稱賀。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xining, Shenzong honored Empress Dowager Cao as grand empress dowager; proceeding to Wende Hall he knelt and presented the jade patent to Acting Grand Commandant Zeng Gongliang and the gold seal to Acting Minister over the Masses Han Jiang; again kneeling he presented the jade patent of Empress Dowager Gao to Acting Grand Commandant Wen Yanbo and the gold seal to Acting Minister over the Masses Zhao Bian; when the rites were complete, the hundred officials offered congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: In Xining 2, 1069, Shenzong honored Empress Dowager Cao as grand empress dowager. At Wende Hall he knelt and presented the jade patent to Acting Grand Commandant Zeng Gongliang and the gold seal to Acting Minister over the Masses Han Jiang. He knelt again and presented the jade patent of Empress Dowager Gao to Acting Grand Commandant Wen Yanbo and the gold seal to Acting Minister over the Masses Zhao Bian. When the rites were complete, all officials offered congratulations.

sentences.zh: 哲宗即位，詔尊太后高氏為太皇太后，皇后向氏為皇太后，德妃朱氏為皇太妃。

translations.literal: When Zhezong ascended the throne, an edict honored the empress dowager Gao as grand empress dowager, the empress Xiang as empress dowager, and Virtuous Consort Zhu as imperial consort dowager.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhezong ascended the throne, an edict honored Empress Dowager Gao as grand empress dowager, Empress Xiang as empress dowager, and Virtuous Consort Zhu as imperial consort dowager.

sentences.zh: 禮部議：“皇太妃生日節序物色，其冠服之屬如皇后例，稱慈旨，慶賀用箋。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Rites deliberated: "On the imperial consort dowager's birthday, seasonal gifts and items, and her caps and robes and the like, follow the empress's precedent; she is addressed as 'benevolent decree'; congratulatory communications use the letter form.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites deliberated: "On the imperial consort dowager's birthday, seasonal gifts, and her caps and robes should follow the empress's precedent. She is addressed as 'benevolent decree,' and congratulatory communications should use the letter form.

sentences.zh: 太皇 太后、皇太后於皇太妃稱賜，皇帝稱奉，百官不稱臣。

translations.literal: The grand empress dowager and empress dowager, toward the imperial consort dowager, use the term 'bestow'; the emperor uses the term 'present'; the hundred officials do not style themselves subjects.
translations.idiomatic: The grand empress dowager and empress dowager use the term 'bestow' when addressing the imperial consort dowager; the emperor uses 'present'; and officials do not style themselves as her subjects.

sentences.zh: 皇帝問皇太妃起居用箋，皇太妃答皇帝用書。”

translations.literal: When the emperor inquired after the imperial consort dowager's health, he used the letter form; when the imperial consort dowager replied to the emperor, she used the document form."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor inquired after the imperial consort dowager's health, he used the letter form; when she replied to the emperor, she used the document form."

sentences.zh: 宰臣請特建太皇太后宮曰崇慶，殿曰崇慶、曰壽康；

translations.literal: Chief ministers requested that a separate palace be specially built for the grand empress dowager, called Chongqing; its halls were called Chongqing and Shoukang;
translations.idiomatic: Chief ministers requested that a separate palace be built for the grand empress dowager, called Chongqing, with halls named Chongqing and Shoukang;

sentences.zh: 皇太后宮 曰隆祐，殿曰隆祐、曰慈徽。

translations.literal: the empress dowager's palace was called Longyou; its halls were called Longyou and Cihui.
translations.idiomatic: and that the empress dowager's palace be called Longyou, with halls named Longyou and Cihui.

sentences.zh: 元祐二年，詔太皇太后受冊依章獻明肅皇后故事，皇太后受冊依熙寧二年故事，皇太妃與皇太后同日受冊，令太常禮官詳 定儀注。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanyou, an edict ordered that the grand empress dowager receive the patent according to the precedent of Empress Dowager Zhangxian Mingsu, that the empress dowager receive the patent according to the precedent of the second year of Xining, that the imperial consort dowager receive the patent on the same day as the empress dowager, and that officials of the Temple of Rites be ordered to determine the ceremonial regulations in detail.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanyou 2, 1087, an edict ordered that the grand empress dowager receive the patent according to the precedent of Empress Dowager Zhangxian Mingsu, that the empress dowager receive it according to the Xining 2 precedent, and that the imperial consort dowager receive it on the same day as the empress dowager. Officials of the Temple of Rites were ordered to determine the ceremonial regulations in detail.

sentences.zh: 右諫議大夫梁燾請對文德殿，太皇太后曰：“大臣欲行此禮，予意謂必難行。”

translations.literal: Right Remonstrance Grandee Liang Tao requested an audience at Wende Hall; the grand empress dowager said: "The great ministers wish to perform this ceremony; in my view it will surely be difficult to carry out."
translations.idiomatic: Right Remonstrance Grandee Liang Tao requested an audience at Wende Hall. The grand empress dowager said: "The senior ministers wish to perform this ceremony, but in my view it will surely be difficult to carry out."

sentences.zh: 燾對曰：“誠如聖慮，願堅執勿許。

translations.literal: Tao replied: "It is truly as Your Sacred Majesty considers; I wish firmly to hold to this and not grant permission.
translations.idiomatic: Tao replied: "It is truly as Your Majesty considers. I urge you to hold firm and not grant permission.

sentences.zh: 且母後權同聽政，蓋出一時不得已之 事，乞速罷之。”

translations.literal: Moreover, the empress dowager's co-regency in governing was a matter born of temporary necessity; I beg that it be quickly abolished."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the empress dowager's co-regency was a temporary measure born of necessity. I beg that it be ended at once."

sentences.zh: 中書舍人曾肇亦言：“太皇太后聽政以來，止於延和殿，受遼使朝見，亦止於禦崇政殿，未嚐踐外朝。

translations.literal: Secretariat Drafter Zeng Zhao also said: "Since the grand empress dowager began hearing government, she has stopped at Yanhe Hall; receiving audiences with Liao envoys also stopped at proceeding to Chongzheng Hall; she has never trodden the outer court.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat Drafter Zeng Zhao also said: "Since the grand empress dowager began hearing government, she has remained at Yanhe Hall. Even when receiving audiences with Liao envoys she has proceeded only to Chongzheng Hall and has never entered the outer court.

sentences.zh: 今皇帝述仁祖故事，以極崇奉之禮，太皇太 後儻以此時特下明詔，發揚皇帝孝敬之誠，而固執謙德，止於崇政殿受冊，則皇帝之孝愈顯，太皇太后之德愈尊，兩義俱得，顧不美歟？”

translations.literal: Now the emperor recounts the precedent of Emperor Renzong and uses the utmost ceremony of exalted service; if the grand empress dowager at this time specially issued a clear edict, displaying the emperor's filial reverence, yet firmly holding to modest virtue and receiving the patent only at Chongzheng Hall, then the emperor's filial piety would be the more displayed, the grand empress dowager's virtue the more honored—both meanings would be obtained; would it not be beautiful?"
translations.idiomatic: Now the emperor follows the precedent of Emperor Renzong and offers the utmost ceremony of exalted service. If the grand empress dowager were at this time to issue a clear edict displaying the emperor's filial reverence while firmly holding to modest virtue and receiving the patent only at Chongzheng Hall, the emperor's filial piety would shine all the more brightly and the grand empress dowager's virtue would be all the more honored. Both aims would be served—would that not be admirable?"

sentences.zh: 太皇太后欣然納之，乃詔 將來受冊止於崇政殿。

translations.literal: The grand empress dowager gladly accepted this, and an edict was issued that in future receipt of the patent would stop at Chongzheng Hall.
translations.idiomatic: The grand empress dowager gladly accepted this, and an edict was issued that in future the patent would be received only at Chongzheng Hall.

sentences.zh: 尋以天旱權罷。

translations.literal: Soon, because of drought, it was temporarily suspended.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, because of drought, the ceremony was temporarily suspended.

sentences.zh: 未幾，太師文彥博等以時雨溥澍，秋稼有望，請舉行冊禮，凡三請乃從。

translations.literal: Before long, Grand Preceptor Wen Yanbo and others, because timely rain had abundantly moistened the earth and the autumn crops gave promise, requested that the patent ceremony be performed; after three requests permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Grand Preceptor Wen Yanbo and others, noting that timely rain had abundantly moistened the earth and the autumn harvest gave promise, requested that the patent ceremony be performed. After three requests, permission was granted.

sentences.zh: 九月六日，發太皇太后冊寶於大慶殿，發皇太后、太 妃冊寶於文德殿，行禮如儀。

translations.literal: On the sixth day of the ninth month, the grand empress dowager's patent and seal were issued at Daqing Hall; the empress dowager's and imperial consort dowager's patents and seals were issued at Wende Hall; the rites were performed according to ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: On the sixth day of the ninth month, the grand empress dowager's patent and seal were issued at Daqing Hall, and the empress dowager's and imperial consort dowager's patents and seals were issued at Wende Hall. The rites were performed according to ceremony.

sentences.zh: 紹聖元年，詔：“奉太皇太后旨，皇太妃特與立宮殿名，坐六龍輿，張糸散，出入由宣德正門。”

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaosheng, an edict said: "Following the grand empress dowager's instructions, the imperial consort dowager was specially granted establishment of palace and hall names, seating in the six-dragon carriage, deployment of silk streamers, and entry and exit through the Xuande Main Gate."
translations.idiomatic: In Shaosheng 1, 1094, an edict read: "Following the grand empress dowager's instructions, the imperial consort dowager was specially granted her own palace and hall names, the use of the six-dragon carriage, deployment of silk streamers, and entry and exit through the Xuande Main Gate."

sentences.zh: 有司請應宮中並依稱臣妾，外命婦入內準此；

translations.literal: The relevant offices requested that within the palace all should address her as subject and consort accordingly; titled ladies from outside entering within should follow this standard;
translations.idiomatic: The relevant offices requested that within the palace all should address her as subject and consort, and that titled ladies from outside entering the palace should follow the same standard;

sentences.zh: 百官拜箋稱賀，稱殿下。

translations.literal: the hundred officials, bowing and submitting letters, offered congratulations, addressing her as "Your Highness."
translations.idiomatic: and that officials, bowing and submitting letters of congratulation, should address her as "Your Highness."

sentences.zh: 徽宗即位，加哲宗太妃號曰聖瑞，既又禦文德殿，冊命元符皇后劉氏為太后，並依皇后禮製。

translations.literal: When Huizong ascended the throne, he added to Zhezong's imperial consort dowager the title Shengrui; afterward he also proceeded to Wende Hall and by patent appointed Empress Liu of the Yuanfu era as empress dowager; all followed the empress's ritual regulations.
translations.idiomatic: When Huizong ascended the throne, he added the title Shengrui to Zhezong's imperial consort dowager. He then proceeded to Wende Hall and by patent appointed Empress Liu of the Yuanfu era as empress dowager, all according to the empress's ritual regulations.

sentences.zh: 建炎元年五月，冊元祐皇后為隆祐太后，令所司擇日奉上冊寶，時方巡幸，不克行禮；

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the first year of Jianyan, the empress of the Yuanyou era was patented as Empress Dowager Longyou; the relevant offices were ordered to choose a day and present the patent and seal; at the time the court was on tour and could not perform the ceremony;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Jianyan 1, 1127, the empress of the Yuanyou era was patented as Empress Dowager Longyou, and the relevant offices were ordered to choose a day and present the patent and seal. At the time the court was on tour and could not perform the ceremony;

sentences.zh: 遙尊韋賢妃為宣和皇后。

translations.literal: from afar Lady Wei the Worthy Consort was honored as Empress Xuanhe.
translations.idiomatic: from afar Worthy Consort Wei was honored as Empress Xuanhe.

sentences.zh: 紹興七年三月，詔略曰：“宣和皇后夙擁慶羨，是 生眇衝，乃骨肉之至親，偕父兄而時邁。

translations.literal: In the third month of the seventh year of Shaoxing, an edict in summary said: "Empress Xuanhe long possessed blessed favor; thereby was born the young sovereign; she is kin of flesh and bone in the utmost degree; together with father and elder brothers she departed in season.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Shaoxing 7, 1137, an edict in summary read: "Empress Xuanhe long enjoyed blessed favor and thereby bore the young sovereign. She is our closest kin by blood, yet departed with her father and elder brothers in their time.

sentences.zh: 十年地阻，懷《陟岵》、《凱風》之思；

translations.literal: Ten years the land blocked us; we cherish the thoughts of 《Ascending the Hill》 and 《Balmy Breeze》;
translations.idiomatic: For ten years the land lay between us, and we cherish the longing expressed in 《Ascending the Hill》 and 《Balmy Breeze》;

sentences.zh: 萬里使還，奉上皇、寧德之諱。

translations.literal: an envoy returned ten thousand li and presented the posthumous names of the Retired Emperor and Ningde.
translations.idiomatic: an envoy returned from ten thousand li and brought word of the posthumous names of the Retired Emperor and Ningde.

sentences.zh: 宜尊為皇太后，令所司擇日奉上冊寶。”

translations.literal: She should be honored as empress dowager; the relevant offices are ordered to choose a day and present the patent and seal."
translations.idiomatic: She should be honored as empress dowager, and the relevant offices are ordered to choose a day and present the patent and seal."

sentences.zh: 太常寺 言：“請依祖宗故事，俟三年之喪終製，然後行禮。”

translations.literal: The Temple of Rites said: "We request following the ancestral precedent, waiting until the three-year mourning is fully completed, and then performing the ceremony."
translations.idiomatic: The Temple of Rites reported: "We request following ancestral precedent and waiting until the three-year mourning is fully completed before performing the ceremony."

sentences.zh: 時翰林學士朱震言：“唐德宗建中上太后沈氏尊號時，沈太后莫知所在，猶供張含元殿，具袞冕，出左序，立 東方，再拜奉冊。
